anchors.paper_title: EEG data of motor imagery for stroke
anchors.reason: The candidate is the figshare record (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.7636301) by Tianyu Jia, the same source DOI listed in the dataset. It describes the motor imagery EEG data from stroke patients, so it is another deposit of the same data.

anchors.paper_title: PA-TCNet: Pathology-Aware Temporal Calibration with Physiology-Guided Target Refinement for Cross-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding in Stroke Patients
anchors.reason: PA-TCNet (2026) proposes a cross-subject decoding method for stroke motor-imagery EEG and likely uses this dataset. It does not introduce or release the Jia 2019 data.

anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, not a paper describing the Jia2019 stroke motor-imagery dataset.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard/specification used to format the dataset, not a paper describing the stroke motor-imagery recordings.

metadata.methods_description: Cue-based left- vs right-hand motor imagery paradigm in stroke patients, where one hand is paretic and the other unaffected. EEG was recorded from 63 channels at 512 Hz with 50 Hz line frequency, in one session of two runs per subject, 40 trials per class, with trial interval 0-6.8 s. Data are preprocessed and epoched.
